title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
claim: In 3d–Gd(III) clusters, Gd(III) weakens the usually strong 3d–3d exchange, and a higher unpaired-electron density still tracks a larger gravimetric −ΔSM, but antiferromagnetic coupling and transition-metal crystal-field effects can cut the observed entropy well below the spin-only limit.
explanation: Figure 9 is the heterometallic analogue of the Gd-only density plot at ΔH = 70 kOe. Heavy-ligand Gd24Co16 and Gd24Cu36 give small −ΔSM values (26.0 and 21.0 J kg−1 K−1), while lighter acetate and more Gd(III) raise it (Gd24Zn4 31.4, Gd36Ni12 36.3, Gd42Ni10 38.2, Gd42Co10 41.3 J kg−1 K−1). Gd96Ni64 reaches 42.8 J kg−1 K−1, the largest cited for 3d–Gd clusters. Gd36Ni12 is only about half of its 64.8 J kg−1 K−1 theoretical value; Gd42Ni10 exceeds it slightly because weaker antiferromagnetism (θ = −3.79 K versus −3.95 K) outweighs a lower magnetic density. A slightly larger value for Co(II) versus Ni(II) analogues is attributed to the higher ground-state spin of Co(II).
scope: High-nuclearity 3d–Gd(III) hydroxide clusters intended as cryogenic molecular coolers.
conditions: Gravimetric −ΔSM at ΔH = 70 kOe; comparisons among acetate-supported Ni/Co/Zn/Cu–Gd clusters and larger Ni–Gd clusters.
caveats: The Co versus Ni spin argument is a suggested interpretation for one pair. Crystal-field and antiferromagnetic contributions are not separated experimentally for every compound. Some formulas and reference numbers in this section are garbled.
